correctness.rationale: For the Fermat quartic over the unramified three-adic quadratic extension, Hermitian polarization proves every special line is defined over the nine-element field and counts exactly 112. The 48 classical pairing lines lift by Hensel, while the 64-line monomial orbit of the explicitly parametrized line has an uncancellable coefficient 12 modulo nine. The normal bundle of every line is O(-2), giving reduced zero-dimensional fibers. Proper plus quasi-finite makes the Fano scheme finite; each completed local algebra has reduced residue k and, by cyclic Nakayama, is R or R/(3^n). This reduces the complete local-scheme classification to lifting versus nonlifting modulo nine. Frobenius-fixed-line counting gives eight rational vertical components and the stated quadratic orbits. The program independently enumerates all 112 F9 lines and their tangent ranks. Boundary: only the stated fixed equation and bases; existence of extra special lines does not mean liftability.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The implication gap is structural: a fieldwise count (even with an incidence graph) is strictly weaker than a complete relative scheme isomorphism. Likewise knowing that only 48 lines exist in characteristic zero does not prove that an extra char-three line lacks a lift modulo nine; the latter requires an explicit first-order calculation.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete arithmetic classification of a distinguished, much-studied K3 line configuration. It explains scheme-theoretically how the geometric number of lines jumps from 48 to 112 on a smooth special fiber, proves all extra lines die at first order rather than having nilpotent mixed-characteristic thickness, and supplies the exact residue-field arithmetic over the original base. The finite local decomposition is more informative than line counts or numerical incidence, and the mod-nine obstruction identifies a genuine deformation boundary; it is not an arbitrary extra finite table.
